藏傳長號（Dungchen）是西藏與蒙古佛教儀式使用的長號角，亦稱「筒欽」或「r: The dungchen is a long horn used in Tibetan and Mongolian Buddhist ritual, also called tongqin or rag dung, whose literal senses are “great horn” and “copper horn”. It belongs among lip-reed aerophones, in the horn and brass class, sounds by the vibration of the player's lips, and is usually played in pairs or in larger groups. Its voice is likened to an elephant's call, and it is one of the most widely used instruments in Tibetan Buddhist culture.
